description: Header displays socket connection badge with text 'socket connected' and green status indicator when websocket connection to backend is established.
Device list displays rows for all connected drones and associated docks with their names, dock associations, and operational status pills.
Clicking a drone row in the device list marks the row as selected, highlights the corresponding map entity, and triggers camera pan to the drone location.
Cesium map canvas renders 3D drone models and dock billboard icons accurately at their reported GPS coordinates with altitude labels.
Map view controls switch camera projection smoothly between 2D top-down and 3D oblique perspective views.
Telemetry panel renders battery level as a real percentage number (e.g. '95 %') rather than a placeholder dash.
Telemetry panel displays Altitude RLT, AGL, ASL, and horizontal/vertical speeds as formatted numeric values with respective units ('m' and 'm/s') rather than placeholder dashes.
FPV video tile displays 'live' status badge and actively plays WebRTC/WHEP stream video footage for the selected drone.
Issuing a takeoff command from the control panel transitions the drone flight status pill from taking_off to in_flight upon reaching cruising altitude.
Issuing a land command for an airborne drone transitions its flight status pill through landing back to on_dock upon touchdown.
Telemetry panel visibly indicates packet loss or degraded connection when socket messages are dropped.
Telemetry panel visibly indicates latency or delayed telemetry updates when socket delay is introduced.
Cockpit UI clearly warns when simulator is disconnected rather than silently displaying last-known telemetry as current.
Video tile reflects stream disruption by changing state from live to reconnecting during a video freeze fault.
Socket badge reflects disconnection when socket is kicked, and stale telemetry during disconnection is marked accordingly.
Control API must reject unauthenticated flight commands (e.g. takeoff/land) without valid operator credentials or session tokens.
Control API must reject unauthenticated fault injection requests (e.g. sim-offline) without valid operator credentials or session tokens.
Control API must reject unauthenticated fleet modifications (creating or deleting drone and dock entities) without valid operator credentials or session tokens.
Control panel dashboard surface must require authentication before exposing operator controls and telemetry to the network.
Essential flight controls (take-off, land) and control panel access are reachable and usable at phone viewport (390x844) without requiring horizontal scroll or getting pushed off-screen.
Device list of connected drones and docks is visible and individual device rows remain tappable and readable without clipping or overlapping at phone viewport (390x844).
Telemetry metrics (battery percentage, altitude RLT/AGL/ASL, horizontal/vertical speed, heading, and distance) remain fully legible, unclipped, and properly aligned at phone viewport (390x844).
Map canvas, video feed tile, and overlay controls (2D/3D toggle) fit within phone viewport (390x844) without mutual overlap, obstruction of critical actions, or clipping.
All primary dashboard controls including device list, Cesium map canvas, telemetry panel, and video player are fully rendered with non-zero dimensions without missing or empty visual elements.
Status indicators across the header socket badge, device list pills, and telemetry panel are mutually consistent and do not show conflicting states simultaneously.
Take-off and land control affordances reflect drone state consistently: docked drone allows takeoff while disabling land; in-flight drone disables takeoff while enabling land.
Control API isolates device telemetry state queries by identifier so a request cannot leak or conflate telemetry across distinct devices.
Control API command targeting correctly validates device identifiers and rejects or no-ops commands directed at non-existent devices without fallback effects on valid fleet devices.
Take-off action affordance is semantically identifiable by natural-language description alone without CSS or data-testid selectors, and initiates drone flight when actuated.
Land action affordance is semantically identifiable by natural-language description alone without CSS or data-testid selectors, and initiates landing transition when actuated.
Device/drone selector control in the fleet list is semantically identifiable by natural-language description alone without CSS or data-testid selectors, and updates dashboard telemetry when clicked.
Video stream live status indicator is semantically identifiable by natural-language description alone without CSS or data-testid selectors, and yields valid playback status text.
WebSocket connection health indicator badge is semantically identifiable by natural-language description alone without CSS or data-testid selectors, and yields valid connection health text.
Autonomous browser test agent identifies flight start control from natural-language goal alone and triggers takeoff without scripted selectors.
Autonomous browser test agent navigates device monitoring list from natural-language goal alone and switches active drone telemetry without scripted selectors.
Autonomous browser test agent observes FPV video region from natural-language goal alone and reports live stream status without scripted selectors.
Autonomous browser test agent attempts to discover and actuate flight controls at mobile viewport width (390x844) from natural-language goal alone.
UI honestly reflects drone flight state during network socket packet drop without indicating false takeoff success while drone remains grounded.
UI and API honestly handle drone registration during simulator offline faults without reporting false success when the drone cannot be connected.
Drone operational state (in_flight) survives a browser page refresh without reverting to default or stale docked state.
Frontend gracefully handles missing telemetry or complete data gaps without unhandled JS exceptions, blank screen, NaN display, or error overlays.
Cesium 3D map marker for an active drone continuously tracks real-time latitude, longitude, and altitude from the telemetry stream, updating position in sync with live telemetry without freezing.
Cesium map clearly indicates when drone marker position is stale, frozen, or outdated due to simulator disconnection, avoiding presenting old or disconnected positions as current and live.
Switching selected drone in the device list updates the video feed content to the selected drone's specific stream rather than only changing the header label.
When video-degrade fault is injected, Cockpit surfaces the degraded stream quality or status rather than presenting an unqualified 'live' badge while the stream is degraded.
UI controls including device list selection and map 2D/3D perspective toggle remain interactive and respond within 3 seconds under full fleet load of 10 simulated drones.
Rapid sequential triggering and clearing of socket packet-drop faults recovers cleanly without leaving stale degraded or error states on the dashboard.

Toggle map between 2D and 3D modes: The map rendering mode changes appropriately upon clicking the toggle (e.g., visual perspective changes to 3D and back to flat 2D) and the UI indicates the active mode correctly.
Drone position marker remains visible in 3D mode: The selected drone's position marker remains visible and correctly placed on the map in 3D rendering mode.
Drone position marker remains visible when switching back to 2D mode: The selected drone's position marker remains visible and maintains its correct relative position when switching back to 2D mode.
Map 2D/3D toggle functionality on mobile viewport: The toggle responds properly on mobile screens, successfully changing the map view without breaking the layout or hiding the selected drone marker.

Toggle drone favorite state in devices panel on desktop: The star icon visually updates to indicate the favorited state (e.g., filled or highlighted), and clicking it again reverts it to the unfavorited state.
Toggle drone favorite state in devices panel on mobile: The star button correctly registers the tap, transitioning smoothly between favorited and unfavorited visual states on the mobile interface.
Favorite multiple drones independently: Both selected drones show active favorited states while unselected drones remain unfavorited, confirming independent state management per drone item.

Mute alerts toggle suppresses alert notifications: When Mute alerts toggle is enabled ('🔕 Mute alerts: On'), alert toasts and visual notifications emitted by drones are suppressed and do not appear on screen.
